summary: Missing final sentence after fast TLS session resume behind nginx HTTP/2 proxy
description:
Issue summary: Customers on ScribeAI are reporting that long streaming responses occasionally finish with a missing final sentence when the client reconnects quickly using TLS session resumption while traffic is routed through an nginx HTTP/2 front proxy.

Impact: Final sentence (often the last punctuated sentence) is truncated or absent from the transcript. This affects end-user experience for ~3% of long streaming sessions (>60s) and is reproducible under specific network/proxy conditions.

Environment: Production (us-west-2), customer on Dedicated plan with private routing through customer-managed nginx gateway; backend Redwood nodes running serving-runtime v2.4.1. Browser clients primarily Chrome 114/115 and iOS app WebView.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a long streaming request that emits multiple SSE events over >60s (prompt with multi-paragraph answer).
2) Client backgrounded for ~1s and then foregrounded immediately (this forces a fast reconnect via TLS session resumption).
3) Client reconnects; nginx on customer side accepts session resumption and multiplexes the new HTTP/2 stream to a different upstream worker behind load-balancer.
4) The resumed stream delivers the remaining tokens but the final sentence punctuation and final event boundary are not delivered to the client; transcript ends abruptly.

Observed behavior: The last sentence is missing; stream appears to end cleanly from the server side (no 5xx), but the client never receives the terminal event marker. Server logs show the final token batch was emitted, but the SSE boundary/event delimiter appears to be coalesced/stripped in transit when HTTP/2 data frames are re-framed by nginx during session resumption.

Expected behavior: Client should receive the full final sentence and the terminal stream marker within the resumed session.

Initial hypotheses:
- nginx HTTP/2 re-framing + proxy_buffering settings can coalesce small frames and drop a trailing newline/event delimiter if the client reconnect and the upstream connection switches mid-stream.
- TLS session resumption + fast reconnect sometimes routes to a different worker with slight KV-cache alignment differences; the runtime assumes the downstream will preserve SSE chunk boundaries.

Immediate mitigation: Advise customer to set 'proxy_buffering off' and 'http2_max_field_size' defaults for testing. A temporary client-side workaround is to append explicit sentinel text at the end of each generation (e.g., "[[END_OF_ANSWER]]") until server-side fix is deployed.

Related links: Slack thread #support-scribeai (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567), customer nginx config snippet provided in attachment, lightweight capture of failing session (S3 link provided to support).

Notes: This ticket captures a production customer reproducible under their nginx+http2 configuration; we should prioritize because it affects user-visible completion integrity.

comments: 2026-03-11 Priya Raman (Support): Customer opened after noticing missing final sentence in ~3% of long streams. Collected nginx config and pcap. Escalating to SRE and Runtime team.
2026-03-11 Ethan Cole (SRE): Acknowledged. Reproduced in staging by simulating TLS resumption + nginx http2. Added to our investigation. See slack thread #support-scribeai.

2026-03-12 Marco Villanueva (Runtime eng): Observed that serving-runtime v2.4.1 emits final "event delimiter" in a separate write call; nginx bundles small writes when proxy_buffering is enabled which can drop an empty frame during HTTP/2 re-framing on fast reconnect. Creating a small integration test to demonstrate. Linked GH issue: gh/issues/4583.

2026-03-12 Laura Becker (Customer CS): Shared customer workaround: disabled proxy_buffering and saw immediate improvement in their canary (0 failures in 200 long streams). Customer prefers a server-side fix.

2026-03-12 Ethan Cole (SRE): Proposed short-term patch: ensure server-side final write coalesces trailing delimiter into previous non-empty write (PR draft gh/pr/1342). Rolling a canary to dedicated infra to validate.
investigation_notes: Repro on staging: reproduce by background/foreground within 500ms while nginx has proxy_buffering on and http2 enabled; failure rate ~7% in synthetic test harness.
nginx config that reproduces failure: proxy_buffering on; proxy_http_version 1.1 with http2 front; observed http2 frame coalescing behavior.

Runtime code path: final delimiter is written via a zero-length write after token stream; zero-length writes are sensitive to proxy coalescing; change will be to append delimiter to last payload write (safe for all transports).
No evidence of token loss at runtime; transmission layer is where delimiter disappears. No 5xx, no client error logs other than missing punctuation in transcript.
next_steps: 1) Merge and canary PR gh/pr/1342 to ensure final delimiter is concatenated with last payload (patch ready). 2) Coordinate with ScribeAI to roll patch to their dedicated nodes after canary success. 3) Draft KB article recommending proxy_buffering off or explicit sentinel until fix is rolled. 4) Add automated test in integration suite for fast reconnect + http2 to prevent regressions.
notes: Priority customer, dedicated infra. Patch targets safe behavior change (concatenate delimiter). Will monitor canary metrics for 48 hours post-rollout.
